entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I see... So there are eight different[n]ways to roast coffee beans. Apparently[n]the light roast is the most acidic.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: It says here that the type of roast[n]you want should differ depending on[n]how you want to drink your coffee.
That's fascinating.[clr 27]
You're so studious.
Can you make some for me?[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: It is. I think I'd like to try[n]hand-roasting each type someday.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Thank you. I'd like to make sure[n]the beans I'm growing can reach[n]their full potentials.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: *giggle* I'd rather not. I don't think[n]I could ever hope to match the intense[n]depth of Sakura-san's coffee.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: You know, Okumura Foods didn't[n]start out as a burger chain...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Originally it was nothing more than[n]a small café run by my grandfather.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: That particular shop closed before[n]I was old enough to appreciate the[n]finer intricacies of coffee...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: But that's where the real origin[n]of our family business lies.
I had no idea.[clr 27]
That's a surprise.
I could've guessed that.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I didn't either. My father only first[n]mentioned it to me a year or two ago.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Yes. After all, everyone knows[n]the company for its burgers.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Really? But we only serve[n]instant coffee at Big Bang.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: At any rate, after my grandfather passed,[n]the company shut the café down due to[n]its steady loss of revenue.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: He had never cared about turning[n]a profit though. His only goal[n]was to make people happy.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: He built a strong community around[n]the café... He'd even give out free[n]meals to those who couldn't afford it.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Then the day it closed, people[n]lined up for blocks to give flowers.[n]They really loved that place...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I wonder how many people would[n]line up for Big Bang Burger if it[n]suddenly went out of business...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I know we need to do well to keep our[n]employees paid, but I can't help but[n]think we've lost something important.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I mean, Takakura-san seems to only[n]be focused on profits... At this rate,[n]we'll never lose our black image.
You might be right.
That would be bad.
Black like coffee?[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Is there really nothing I can do...?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: The company name is just going to[n]keep getting dragged through the mud...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Yeah... I have to figure out a[n]way I can turn things around.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: ...Huh?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Oh, I get it!

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: *giggle* You're so funny,[n][fName]-kun!

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: You were trying to cheer me up,[n]weren't you...? Thanks for that.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: *sigh* I think what I really[n]need... is to get stronger.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I mean, I can act tough in front of my[n]employees... but you know how weak[n]I am inside.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: ...I have a plan though.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Before I can really determine who I[n]trust, I first need to know what it[n]means to have others trust in me.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: So, I'm going to get stronger...[n]strong enough for you and the[n]others to rely on me!
I can sense a strong[n]resolve from Haru...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Hm... but how am I supposed to[n]gain the trust of my employees?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I'm not great at public speaking...[n]and even just giving my opinion[n]makes me a little nervous...

entries.speaker: Man's Voice
entries.en: Haru?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: S-Sugimura-san...!? What are you[n]doing here?

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: I was just heading home from[n]a business engagement when I[n]saw you from my car window.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: Hm? Do I know you from somewhere?

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: You're one of those brats from before...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Um, this is a friend from school. He's[n]helping me look for some books today.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Anyway, we should be getting back[n]to our shopping. Please excuse us.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: ...Hold on, Haru. You think you can[n]go on a date with another man and[n]leave your fiancé in the dust?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: You are not my fiancé... I already[n]said, I'm not going to marry you.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: Oh yeah? And what about the[n]contract I made with your father?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: F-Father is... no longer here...[n]Besides, marriage is something you[n]go into with your own free will...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: A contract could never[n]hold the same weight...

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: Are you sure about that? Think about[n]the reparations clause.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: If you back out of the deal now,[n]you will lose everything you own.[n]Okumura Foods, your estate...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Even so, I...

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: And what about your employees? Are you[n]really willing to put their jobs on the[n]line for the sake of your selfishness?

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: Besides, this marriage is exactly[n]what Okumura Foods needs right now.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: My father would have no trouble[n]managing your shares or sweeping[n]away your company's tarnished image.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: That reminds me, did Takakura-san[n]tell you about the wedding hall? He[n]got us the Phoenix Wing at the Wilton.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Wh-What!?

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: He made a provisional reservation[n]for ten days this coming spring.[n]After all, the sooner the better.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: W-Wait a minute!

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: We'll have to look into our guests'[n]schedules as well. There'll be over[n]three hundred of them, you know.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: Takakura-san can handle Okumura Foods[n]in the meantime. Why don't you go stop[n]by the gym or something, Haru?

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: I mean, if you have time to mess[n]around with this punk, you damn well[n]have time to get a little thinner.

entries.speaker: Haru's Fiancé
entries.en: I'm out of here.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: I'm sorry about that...
You don't need to apologize.
That guy is horrible.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: You're not wrong about that...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: He has everything... Fame,[n]intelligence, etiquette...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: The only thing he needs now[n]is a wife he can control...

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: And I guess I'm the perfect target.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: He's going to get Okumura Foods as[n]well as my entire inheritance... and[n]I'm totally powerless against him...
You're not powerless.
Be strong, Haru.[clr 27]

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Oh, sorry. I practically[n]forced you to say that.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: But... thank you.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: You're right... I can't afford to drag[n]myself down with such negativity.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: ...Thank you.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Anyway, um, I hope I can share[n]with you again some other time.

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: For today though... I'm rather tired.[n]Would it be okay if we parted here?

entries.speaker: Haru
entries.en: Well, goodbye.
